Bug_Details:
Calling getClass() on an object of type Class returns the Class object for java.lang.Class; you probably meant to operate on the object directly Calling getClass() on an object of type Class returns the Class object for
java.lang.Class. Usually this is a mistake, and people intend to operate on the
object itself (for example, to print an error message). If you really did intend
to operate on the Class object for java.lang.Class, please use Class.class
instead for clarity.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by calling getClass() on an object of type Class, which returns the Class object for java.lang.Class instead of the intended Class object.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug method with String.class as an argument. Inside the showBug method, clazz.getClass().getName() is called, which triggers the bug by returning 'java.lang.Class' instead of 'java.lang.String'. This causes the assertion to fail, thus triggering the bug.
